name: tower
renderNote: Layers, shares, figures and the key are one `<svg>`. Every layer is the same height, not drawn to scale: its size is printed beside it in the market's notation (`$40M xs $50M`) and each boundary carries its figure on the right edge, so a $40M bottom layer stays as readable as a $200M top one.

projection.frame: each layer sits on the one below it, split across the reinsurers who took a share of it

description: A reinsurance program as stacked layers, each written as its limit in excess of its attachment and split across the reinsurers who took a share of it.
purpose: Use for a reinsurance or insurance tower — a catastrophe program, a casualty excess tower, a D&O program. The retention sits at the bottom, each layer above it is labeled in the market's notation (`$40M xs $50M`), and each layer is split into its reinsurers' shares, one color per reinsurer across every layer, with any unplaced share shown as `Open`.

title.description: Slide heading — say what the structure means for the client ('A $50M retention saves $3.7M'), not 'Program structure'.

layers.description: One li per layer: the layer name, then a trailing inline-code size in the market's notation — `Layer 2 \`$70M xs $90M\`` (limit, then `xs`, `x/s` or `excess of`, then attachment). A size with no `xs` is the retention, the band from zero to that figure. Any order: the chart sorts by attachment, lowest at the bottom.

shares.description: Optional nested bullets under a layer, one per reinsurer: `Acme Re \`30%\``. Each reinsurer keeps one color across every layer. Shares that add up to less than 100% leave the rest as an `Open` segment; a layer with no shares is drawn plain.

whenToUse.title: The structure is the decision
whenToUse.body: A tower earns its slide when the conversation is about the program's shape — where the retention sits, how the layers stack, which reinsurers carry which part. For the cost of each layer, use `stacked-bar` or `bar`; for how losses would hit it, use `waterfall`.

whenToUse.title: Two to six layers
whenToUse.body: Every layer is the same height, so the bands thin as layers are added. Past six, merge the thin top layers or split the program across two slides.

whenToUse.title: Up to six reinsurers
whenToUse.body: Each reinsurer keeps one color across every layer. A seventh and beyond fold into one `Others` color, summed per layer, so name the ones the client will ask about.

antiPatterns.title: Reading the height as the size
antiPatterns.body: The layers are drawn at equal height on purpose, so a $40M layer and a $200M layer look the same size. When the audience needs to SEE the size difference, show the limits as a `bar` chart instead.

antiPatterns.title: Shares that are dollars
antiPatterns.body: A share is a percentage of its layer. Write the reinsurer's line as `30%`, not `$12M`: a dollar figure reads as 12 million percent.

related.name: stacked-bar
related.when: the premium or cost of each layer, compared on a scale

related.name: waterfall
related.when: how a loss or a result walks from one total to another

related.name: table
related.when: the full placement slip, with every line and every term

commonMistakes.mistake: Writing the layer as attachment then limit (`$50M xs $40M` for a $40M layer sitting at $50M).
commonMistakes.fix: The market's order is LIMIT xs ATTACHMENT: `$40M xs $50M` is $40M of cover above $50M. The chart reads it that way, so the reversed form draws the wrong boundaries.

dataShapeGuidance: A layer's size reads like every chart number (lib/core/chart-values.js), on both sides of `xs`: `$40M`, `USD 40mn`, `EUR 40 Mio.` and `40,000,000` all mean the same.
Shares are percentages of the layer. Under 100% leaves an `Open` segment; over 100% is drawn scaled to the layer and the description says it is over-placed.

budget.note: Counted in LAYERS (top-level items; the shares nest under them). Editorial: every layer is the same height, so the bands thin as layers are added, and past six on a full slide the name and notation no longer fit beside a band.

pane.review: side 25 measured, 35 reviewed: the key cramps at 25%, as stacked-bar's does; stack 30 measured, 50 reviewed: a tower in a band under half the stage thins every layer to a sliver.

venueCapacity.none: A chart scales its marks to the box instead of clipping, so no count marks where it stops fitting.
